subject: design-technology
source_note: Topic structure follows the National Curriculum KS3 programme of study for Design & Technology. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Design
units.blurb: Researching needs and generating creative design ideas

units.name: Make
units.blurb: Using specialist tools, materials and components to make products

units.name: Evaluate
units.blurb: Testing, refining and judging the impact of design and technology

units.name: Technical Knowledge
units.blurb: Materials, mechanical, electrical and programmable systems

topics.name: Understanding User Needs
topics.blurb: Using research and exploration, such as different cultures, to identify user needs

topics.name: Design Problems
topics.blurb: Identifying, solving and reformulating design problems

topics.name: Developing Specifications
topics.blurb: Writing specifications for innovative, functional, appealing products

topics.name: Generating Creative Ideas
topics.blurb: Using approaches such as biomimicry and user-centred design to avoid stereotypes

topics.name: Communicating Design Ideas
topics.blurb: Annotated sketches, plans, 3-D and mathematical modelling and digital presentations

topics.name: Specialist Tools & CAM
topics.blurb: Using specialist tools, processes and computer-aided manufacture precisely

topics.name: Materials & Components
topics.blurb: Selecting a complex range of materials, components and ingredients by their properties

topics.name: Analysing the Work of Others
topics.blurb: Analysing past and present professionals to broaden understanding

topics.name: New & Emerging Technologies
topics.blurb: Investigating technologies that are new to designers and makers

topics.name: Testing & Refining
topics.blurb: Testing and refining products against a specification and users' views

topics.name: Impact of Design & Technology
topics.blurb: How design and technology affects people, society, the environment and designers' responsibilities

topics.name: Materials & Structures
topics.blurb: Properties of materials and the performance of structural elements

topics.name: Mechanical Systems
topics.blurb: More advanced systems that change movement and force

topics.name: Electrical & Electronic Systems
topics.blurb: Powering and using circuits with heat, light, sound and movement

topics.name: Programmable Components
topics.blurb: Embedding intelligence with sensors, actuators and microcontrollers

connections.why: Understanding users helps you frame the right design problem to solve
A clear problem is turned into measurable design specifications
The specification sets the brief that creative ideas must satisfy
Ideas are developed by drawing, modelling and presenting them
Detailed plans guide the tools and processes used to make the product
Design ideas determine which materials and components are chosen
Tools and processes are matched to the materials being worked
Choosing materials well requires understanding their properties and structures
Products are tested and refined against the original specification
Evaluating others' work informs how you judge and improve your own
New technologies raise questions about their impact and designers' responsibilities
Emerging electronics make it possible to embed intelligence in products
Knowing how structures perform guides how they are made
Programmable components control actuators that drive mechanical movement
Inputs and outputs in circuits are coordinated by programmable components
The materials chosen are validated when the product is tested
Reformulating a problem keeps the focus on the real user need
